name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping
juice and zest of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons
1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

writer_notes: Source (eatingbirdfood.com) is a 4-serving recipe; locked view is a clean 3.5x scale to 14 servings. All quantities reconcile.
All 20 locked ingredient lines are used by a step; no orphaned buys and no step uses anything unbought.
Water (7 cups) is not among the costed lines, as expected for tap water; noted only for completeness.
Jalapeno kept optional in prose per the source, but it is still a bought/costed line so the shopper acquires it.
Cotija and cilantro each carry a salad quantity plus a topping quantity in the buy strings; both portions are accounted for in the steps.
No cost_lines were supplied in this dispatch, so no package arithmetic claims were made; only the ${{cost_ps}} token and package-size references are used for money.
165F cook temp and ~20 min rice come from the transcription (cooking temp/time, not macros/costs) and are safe to state.
Macros in band: 597 cal (under 600), 44.6 g protein (>=40), carbs unrestricted, chicken breast protein, real carb (rice), no seafood.

prose.intro_html:
Mexican street corn, or elote, is one of those foods that tastes like a treat and costs like a side dish. We took that creamy, tangy, lime-forward corn and built a whole meal-prep dinner around it: seasoned chicken breast, cilantro lime rice, and a scoop of that street corn salad piled on top. It eats like something you would order out, and it lands at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, which is the whole point.

Here is the honest part. Nothing here is fancy. Canned corn, a block of cotija, a bag of rice, and chicken breast on sale. What makes it feel special is the finishing: fresh lime, cilantro, and a little heat. That is where the flavor comes from, and it costs pennies. We are stretching this to 14 containers, so the small stuff goes a long way.
prose.shop_smart:
Buy the chicken breast when it is the loss leader, not when you happen to need it. This batch calls for a little under 5 pounds, so a family pack is exactly the right size and you are not paying convenience pricing on a small tray.

Canned corn is your friend here. The recipe uses drained whole kernel corn, and cans hold their price better than the produce aisle does in the off season. Grab enough to cover 7 cups drained and you are set. If sweet corn is in season and cheap, fresh works too, you just cook and cut it off the cob first.

Cotija comes as a block or a crumbled tub. Either fits this recipe, so buy whichever the store has priced better that week. It is a salty finishing cheese, so a little carries a lot of flavor. Same story with the limes: you need juice and zest from three and a half limes plus extra for finishing, so pick up a small bag rather than singles. Greek yogurt does the heavy lifting that sour cream usually would, and plain 2 percent keeps the protein up without the extra fat.
prose.make_it:
Start the rice. Bring the water to a boil, then add the rice and sea salt. Cover, drop the heat to low, and simmer until the rice is tender, about 20 minutes. While it cooks, stir the chopped cilantro together with the lime juice and lime zest in a big bowl. When the rice is done and still warm, tip it into that bowl and toss so every grain picks up the lime and cilantro.

Mix the street corn salad. In a large bowl combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, the diced jalapeno if you want the heat, chopped cilantro, and the salt. Stir gently until it comes together, taste, and adjust the salt or lime. Set it aside so the flavors get friendly.

Season and sear the chicken. In a small bowl stir together the chili powder, sea salt, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and onion powder. Toss the 1-inch chicken chunks in that spice blend until they are coated. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium, and once it is hot add the chicken. Cook 4 to 5 minutes per side until it is cooked through and the internal temperature hits 165F. Work in two batches if your skillet is crowded, because crowded chicken steams instead of browning.

Build the bowls. Spread a base of the warm cilantro lime rice, top it with the chicken chunks, add a generous scoop of the street corn salad, then finish with cubed avocado, sliced red onion, a little more cotija and cilantro, and a squeeze of fresh lime.
prose.portion_html:
Here is the trick that keeps 14 containers honest: weigh the pot, do not eyeball the scoop. Once the rice, the chicken, and the corn salad are all made, put your empty container on the scale and zero it out. Weigh the full pot of rice, divide by 14, and that is your rice number per container. Do the same for the chicken and again for the corn salad. Now every box gets the same base, the same protein, and the same scoop, and nobody opens day 12 to find they ran short.

Avocado, red onion, extra cotija and cilantro are add-at-serving toppings. Cube the avocado fresh the morning you eat it so it does not brown in the fridge, and keep the sliced onion and a lime wedge on the side. That keeps the bowls bright all week instead of going soggy by Wednesday.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Run the numbers and this comes out to ${{cost_ps}} a serving. That is a restaurant-style bowl, the kind a fast casual place charges you double digits for, made 14 times over for the price of one of theirs.

The chicken is the biggest line on the receipt, which is exactly why you buy it on sale and in the family pack. Everything else, the rice, the canned corn, the yogurt and mayo, the spices, is cheap by nature and stretches across all 14 boxes. The cotija and lime are the splurge, and they are measured in tablespoons and wedges, so the splurge is tiny.

Eat this instead of a {{cal}}-calorie takeout bowl and you are ahead on money and macros at the same time, with {{protein}} grams of protein doing the work.
